technique.how: Ask the patient (or witnesses) whether they have had chills and grade the worst episode: mild = feeling cold, needing a jacket; moderate = needing a thick blanket; shaking chills = whole-body shaking even under a thick blanket. Record timing relative to fever and any line, procedure or infusion.
technique.prerequisites: Patient or witness able to describe the episode; ask before antipyretics blunt recall.

interpretation.positive_finding: Shaking (rigor-grade) chills raise the probability of bacteremia about 4.7-fold (LR+ 4.7, 95% CI 3.0-7.2; specificity 0.90) and justify blood cultures before antibiotics.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of any chills lowers the probability of bacteremia (LR- 0.24) but does not exclude it, particularly in elderly or immunocompromised patients who may not mount rigors.
interpretation.pitfalls: Rigors also occur with malaria, transfusion or drug reactions, and after amphotericin or contaminated infusions; the grading relies on patient recall and the RCE data exclude immunocompromised patients and suspected endocarditis.
interpretation.changes_what: Shaking chills should prompt blood cultures and a search for a bacteremic source (line, biliary, urinary, endovascular); no chills supports withholding cultures when pretest probability is low.

estimates.population: Adult immunocompetent patients in whom bacteremia was suspected (35 studies; 4566 bacteremia and 25,946 negative episodes)
estimates.quote: The severity of chills graded on an ordinal scale (shaking chills, LR, 4.7; 95% CI, 3.0-7.2) may be more useful.

estimates.target_condition: Bacteremia - finding: shaking chills (whole-body shaking under a thick blanket)
estimates.population: 526 consecutive adults with acute febrile illness (40, 7.6%, bacteremic)
estimates.quote: Shaking chills showed a specificity of 90.3% (95% CI 89.2-91.5) and positive likelihood ratio of 4.65 (95% CI 2.95-6.86).

estimates.target_condition: Bacteremia - finding: any chills (sensitivity and LR- refer to absence of chills)
estimates.population: 526 consecutive adults with acute febrile illness (40, 7.6%, bacteremic)
estimates.quote: The absence of chills showed a sensitivity of 87.5% (95% CI 74.4-94.5) and negative likelihood ratio of 0.24 (95% CI 0.11-0.51).

sources.citation: Coburn B, Morris AM, Tomlinson G, Detsky AS. Does this adult patient with suspected bacteremia require blood cultures? JAMA. 2012;308(5):502-511.
Tokuda Y, Miyasato H, Stein GH, Kishaba T. The degree of chills for risk of bacteremia in acute febrile illness. Am J Med. 2005;118(12):1417.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: The RCE conclusions do not apply to immunocompromised patients or when endocarditis is suspected; in those groups obtain cultures regardless of chills.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Rigors with hypotension, altered mentation or a central line indicate probable bacteremia/sepsis: cultures, source control and antibiotics within the hour.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: The three-level chill scale relies on patient self-report; reproducibility between interviewers is not reported in the abstracts.

extraction_notes: RCE LR 4.7 (3.0-7.2) for shaking chills from the Coburn 2012 abstract (PMID 22851117; JAMA not OA, table not seen). The RCE value coincides with Tokuda's 4.65, so the pooled entry likely rests on that single study; evidence_level kept as pooled for the RCE row and the caveat is noted here. Tokuda (PMID 16378800; PubMed lists journal year 2006, print citation Am J Med 2005;118:1417) abstract supplies specificity 0.903 and LR+ 4.65 for shaking chills and sensitivity 0.875/LR- 0.24 for any chills; sensitivity of shaking chills itself is not in the abstract. Prevalence 0.076 = 40/526.
